Resolves NO otherwise.

Each file has the columns date,value: one row per date with a published value, sorted by date. Dates are UTC calendar dates (ISO format). Nothing dated on or after the forecast date is included.

## cairo_tmax.csv

Cairo daily maximum 2 m air temperature. Units: degrees C.  
Source: Open-Meteo historical weather API (archive-api.open-meteo.com, ERA5-based reanalysis), no API key.  
Publication: One value per UTC day. The snapshot holds every day before T; the real archive runs a few days behind, so a forecaster on T would have had slightly less. Recent days can be revised when preliminary reanalysis is replaced by the final one.

## cairo_precip.csv

Cairo daily precipitation total. Units: mm.  
Source: Open-Meteo historical weather API (archive-api.open-meteo.com, ERA5-based reanalysis), no API key.  
Publication: One value per UTC day. The snapshot holds every day before T; the real archive runs a few days behind, so a forecaster on T would have had slightly less. Recent days can be revised when preliminary reanalysis is replaced by the final one.

tasks.question_md:
# Will Cairo daily maximum 2 m air temperature (cairo_tmax) end the 7 days from 2026-07-20 to 2026-07-26 higher than it ended the days before 2026-07-20?

Forecast date (today): 2026-07-20  
Horizon: 7 days (2026-07-20 to 2026-07-26)  
Target series: data/cairo_tmax.csv  
Related series: data/cairo_precip.csv

## Resolution criteria

Resolves YES if the last value of cairo_tmax dated on or after 2026-07-20 and on or before 2026-07-26 is strictly greater than the last value of cairo_tmax dated before 2026-07-20. Resolves NO otherwise, including when no value is dated in that window.

## Fine print

Dates are UTC calendar dates. The target series is data/cairo_tmax.csv (columns date,value; degrees C); its rows are as published by the source, and the question resolves on the rows published for the window's dates. resolve.py's outcome(rows, T, horizon) is called with rows = the (datetime.date, float) pairs of the complete cairo_tmax series sorted by date, T = datetime.date(2026, 7, 20) and horizon = 7.

Each file has the columns date,value: one row per date with a published value, sorted by date. Dates are UTC calendar dates (ISO format). Nothing dated on or after the forecast date is included.

## new_york_precip.csv

New York daily precipitation total. Units: mm.  
Source: Open-Meteo historical weather API (archive-api.open-meteo.com, ERA5-based reanalysis), no API key.  
Publication: One value per UTC day. The snapshot holds every day before T; the real archive runs a few days behind, so a forecaster on T would have had slightly less. Recent days can be revised when preliminary reanalysis is replaced by the final one.

## new_york_tmax.csv

New York daily maximum 2 m air temperature. Units: degrees C.  
Source: Open-Meteo historical weather API (archive-api.open-meteo.com, ERA5-based reanalysis), no API key.  
Publication: One value per UTC day. The snapshot holds every day before T; the real archive runs a few days behind, so a forecaster on T would have had slightly less. Recent days can be revised when preliminary reanalysis is replaced by the final one.

tasks.question_md:
# Will New York daily precipitation total (new_york_precip) be at least 1 mm on at least 2 of the 7 days from 2026-07-27 to 2026-08-02?

Forecast date (today): 2026-07-27  
Horizon: 7 days (2026-07-27 to 2026-08-02)  
Target series: data/new_york_precip.csv  
Related series: data/new_york_tmax.csv

## Resolution criteria

Resolves YES if at least k of the dates on or after 2026-07-27 and on or before 2026-08-02 have a value of new_york_precip of at least 1, where k is the median, rounded up to a whole number, of the number of such dates in each of the 52 consecutive 7-day blocks before 2026-07-27 (the latest is 2026-07-20 to 2026-07-26); k = 2. Resolves NO otherwise.

## Fine print

Dates are UTC calendar dates. The target series is data/new_york_precip.csv (columns date,value; mm); its rows are as published by the source, and the question resolves on the rows published for the window's dates. resolve.py's outcome(rows, T, horizon) is called with rows = the (datetime.date, float) pairs of the complete new_york_precip series sorted by date, T = datetime.date(2026, 7, 27) and horizon = 7.
